tagline: The Gulf of Tunis, the Kerkennah and Djerba islands — a Mediterranean coast of marinas, islands and a famous lagoon suburb run.
summary: Tunisia has one of the Mediterranean's densest marina coasts, built around three natural clusters. The Gulf of Tunis wraps the capital, with the cliffside marina of Sidi Bou Said, the ferry-and-yacht port of La Goulette on the Lake Tunis sandbar, and the Gammarth beach strip. The Sahel resort coast to the south chains Yasmine Hammamet, Port El Kantaoui at Sousse and the 400-berth Cap Monastir marina along the Gulf of Hammamet. And Djerba island sits in the shallow Gulf of Gabes to the far south. Each cluster is a tight set of short water hops that today are all done by congested coast road; a fast water shuttle is the natural spine for Tunisia's tourism coast.
why_marine_mobility: Tunisia's coast is a ring of bays, marinas and islands where the road is slow and the sea is direct. Navier's Pioneer II flies the Gulf of Tunis bay hops — La Goulette to Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa — the Sousse–Monastir marina run, and the island shuttles to Kerkennah and Djerba, silent and zero-emission, while the Quanta-LR range opens longer coastal and cross-Mediterranean connections. It is a tourism-and-marina market with proven coastal travel demand.

demand_signals.label: Tunis–La Marsa coastal corridor
demand_signals.note: The historic TGM light rail along the Tunis bay to La Goulette, Carthage and La Marsa shows dense coastal commuter demand paralleling a calm sea.

demand_signals.label: Sahel marinas
demand_signals.note: Port El Kantaoui (Sousse) and Monastir marina anchor a major Mediterranean resort and yachting economy along the Sahel coast.

demand_signals.label: Kerkennah & Djerba islands
demand_signals.note: The Kerkennah islands off Sfax and Djerba in the south are reached by slow vehicle ferries — water-dependent connections ripe for a fast clean tier.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling bay tier across the Gulf of Tunis — La Goulette to Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa/Gammarth — complementing the TGM with a fast sea layer.
Sahel marina-to-marina hops between Port El Kantaoui and Monastir, and island shuttles to Kerkennah off Sfax.
Upgraded Djerba island crossings (Jorf–Ajim) on fast, dry, zero-emission craft replacing slow vehicle ferries.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The bay, marina and island meshes — La Goulette↔Sidi Bou Saïd (~4 nm), Tunis Marine↔La Goulette (~5 nm), La Goulette↔La Marsa/Gammarth (~7 nm), Sousse↔Monastir (~12 nm), Sfax↔Kerkennah (~11 nm), Jorf↔Ajim/Djerba (~1.1 nm) — sit inside the 70 nm all-electric range on calm Mediterranean water off existing marinas.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The coastal network is Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range opens longer line-haul along the Tunisian coast and toward the central-Mediterranean islands without charging dependency.

signature_routes.label: La Goulette ↔ Sidi Bou Saïd / La Marsa (all-electric Gulf of Tunis bay run)
Sousse (Port El Kantaoui) ↔ Monastir (Sahel marina corridor)

transit_planning: For Tunisia's merchant-marine and ports office (OMMP), a marina operator or a Sahel tourism authority: a clean tier across the Tunis bay, the Sahel marinas and the island crossings, off existing marina and ferry infrastructure.
competitive_landscape: Coastal movement is by road and the TGM rail; the islands are served by slow vehicle ferries and the marinas by charters. There is no fast, clean, premium foiling tier across the bay, the marina coast or the island crossings, leaving greenfield room on calm Mediterranean water.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the Office de la Marine Marchande et des Ports (OMMP) and Tunisia's maritime administration. The country's tourism-and-marina investment agenda and calm Mediterranean coast provide a supportive environment for a clean coastal water-transport tier, with heritage zones (Carthage, Sidi Bou Saïd) favouring a quiet, low-wash platform.
seasonality: A long, warm Mediterranean season (April–October) drives resort, marina and island demand, with the coast calm and sheltered through most of the year; peak summer heat favours air-conditioned electric cabins, and the bay-and-island crossings remain largely navigable into the shoulder months.
corridor_shape: Three separate short-hop clusters: Gulf of Tunis (capital), Sahel resort coast (Hammamet-Sousse-Monastir), and Djerba island. Not one continuous corridor.
